## Data Breach

### Adobe BPO breach exposes 13 million records via phished support agent
🔥🔥🔥🔥◯ A threat actor calling itself "Mr. Raccoon" claims to have leaked 13 million Adobe support tickets with personal data, 15,000 employee records, all HackerOne submissions, and internal documents. The breach originated at a third-party BPO firm: a malicious email sent to a BPO employee silently deployed a Remote Access Tool on the victim's machine. Attackers exploited weak controls at the vendor — agents were permitted to export all support tickets in a single bulk request, with no rate limits, alerts, or authorization controls in place, meaning one compromised account could silently exfiltrate the entire dataset, including unpublished vulnerability reports from HackerOne.

Sources: [Google News — cybersecurity](https://news.google.?oc=5), [Security Boulevard](https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/adobes-bpo-breach-one-phished-support-agent-extracted-13-million-records-and-unpublished-vulnerability-reports/), [Cyberpress](https://cyberpress.org/adobe-breach-threat-actor-claims-leak-of-13-million-support-tickets/)

### Origin Energy confirms customer data breach
🔥🔥🔥◯◯ Origin Energy, Australia's largest energy retailer, confirmed there has been unauthorised access and disclosure of some customer data, including personal information as well as some credit card and banking information. The disclosed data includes full names, physical addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers, per SC Media reporting. The incident was disclosed to the market on 23 July 2026, and Origin has secured its systems and engaged authorities.

Sources: [Google News — cybersecurity](https://news.google.?oc=5), [SC Media](https://www.scworld.com/brief/origin-energy-confirms-data-breach-impacting-millions-of-customers), [Bleeping Computer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/australian-energy-provider-origin-says-data-breach-exposes-client-data/)
